name: Koma Ndera
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only classification/atlas mentions (Bennett 1983, Boyd & Pasch 1988, ALCAM 2012, Blench lists); no phonological description located

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2024. Die Gəmme- und die Vere-Sprachen und das Lɔŋto. Klassensprachen des Samba-Duru am oberen Benue und ihre Beziehungen zum Gur. Ein Bericht (with English preface and appendix). Arbeitspapiere des Instituts für Ethnologie und Afrikastudien 208. Mainz: JGU. https://www.ifeas.uni-mainz.de/wp-content/uploads/sites/396/2025/03/
sources.note: Nothing (grep stress/accent/Akzent/Betonung = 0). Sect. 1.4 (pp. 11-12) defines the Damtəm-Gəunəm cluster = 'Koma Damti' (Nigeria: Maani, Bəəri, Komni, Sengri) and 'Koma Ndera' (Cameroon: Liu, Yaru, Gbayru, Gbaŋru, Ləəlu, Zaanu); appendix p. 52 gives Yarəm noun-class tables (sources: field notes 2011-2017 and an unpublished 'Lexique yarəm - français', Mission Catholique Ndintire, corrected 2017). Only prosodic remark, p. 45: transcriptions 'attempt to represent the sounds and tones phonemically... High tones and clear low tones are marked; mid-tones are generally unmarked'. sources.note: Nothing. Classification only (Vere group:... Vɔmnəm (Koma Vomni); Gəunəm Cluster: Yarəm, Lim, Gbaŋrɨm, Baidəm, Zanəm, Ləələm; Damtəm (Koma Damti)). No Koma Ndera document beyond the wordlists; 2019 conference had no Vere/Koma talk.

sources.citation: Kleinewillinghöfer, Ulrich. 2015. Vere Language Group: Comparative Wordlists. Adamawa Languages Project, JGU Mainz. 19 pp. https://www.blogs.uni-mainz.de/fb07-adamawa/files/2015/06/
sources.note: Nothing. Tone-marked 100-item comparative wordlist; the Koma Ndera lects appear as Damtəm (Koma Damti, of Maani, Nigeria), Gə-Lim (Gəunəm of Lii, Cameroon) and Gə-Yarəm (Gəunəm of the Yarú at Gɛɛdɛ, Cameroon). One-page intro on the survey; no note on stress, accent or tone conventions.
